title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 95 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 508–513 (Night 95, continuing directly from nights-94), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 95 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The disguised 'merchants' bring out the chest, and Dhāt al-Dawāhī, blackened and in chains, is taken by Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Sharrukān for a holy man. She recites war verses on Moses' staff, refuses food, prays through the nights, and at last tells the kings and the vizier Dandān her invented story: pride after walking on the sea, years of captivity under the monk Maṭrūḥanā, the patrician Daqyānūs and his beautiful daughter Tamāthīl, and a monastery full of treasure. She urges them to ride to the monastery to seize the girl and the gold. Only Dandān doubts her; the army is sent on to Constantinople while the two kings, the vizier and a hundred horsemen set out with mules and chests. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fifth-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-fifth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ النَّصَارَى الَّذِينَ فِي هَيْئَةِ التُّجَّارِ لَمَّا اخْتَلَى بِهِمْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخُوهُ شَرْكَانُ شَرَحُوا لَهُمَا حَدِيثَ الزَّاهِدِ وَبَكَوْا حَتَّى أَبْكَوْهُمَا وَأَخْبَرُوهُمَا كَمَا عَلَّمَتْهُمُ الْكَاهِنَةُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-naṣārā alladhīna fī hayʾati al-tujjāri lammā ikhtalā bihim ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-akhūhu sharrukānu sharaḥū lahumā ḥadītha al-zāhidi wa-bakaw ḥattā abkawhumā wa-akhbarūhumā kamā ʿallamathumu al-kāhinatu dhātu al-dawāhī
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the Christians who were in the guise of the merchants, when Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān were alone with them, laid-out to the two of them the story of the ascetic, and wept until they made the two of them weep, and told the two of them as the soothsayer Dhāt al-Dawāhī had taught them.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān were alone with the Christians disguised as merchants, these men told them the story of the ascetic, and wept until they had made the two kings weep too, and said everything just as Dhāt al-Dawāhī, the soothsayer, had taught them.
sentences.n: al-kāhina is properly a soothsayer or priestess; here it names the old woman's office among the Christians, whom she has coached. The main verb of the sentence, sharaḥū “they laid out”, comes only after the lammā clause, as is usual in this narrative style.

sentences.t: فَرَّقَ قَلْبُ شَرْكَانَ لِلزَّاهِدِ وَأَخَذَتْهُ الرَّأْفَةُ عَلَيْهِ وَقَامَتْ بِهِ الْحَمِيَّةُ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: farraqa qalbu sharrukāna li-al-zāhidi wa-akhadhathu al-raʾfatu ʿalayhi wa-qāmat bihi al-ḥamiyyatu li-allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And softened the heart of Sharrukān toward the ascetic, and the pity took him over him, and there rose up in him the zeal for God, exalted is He;
sentences.i: Sharrukān's heart softened toward the ascetic; he was seized with pity for him, and zeal for God, the Exalted, rose up in him.
sentences.n: The print puts its shadda on the rāʾ of فرّق, which would make the word farraqa, “he divided”. The sense wants fa-raqqa, “and softened” (raqqa qalbuhu, “his heart grew tender”), with the doubling on the qāf. The printed mark is kept where it stands, and the word is translated as fa-raqqa. al-ḥamiyya is the hot zeal of a man roused to defend what is his, here the faith.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُمْ هَلْ خَلَّصْتُمْ هَذَا الزَّاهِدَ أَمْ هُوَ فِى الدَّيْرِ إِلَى الْآنَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahum hal khallaṣtum hādhā al-zāhida am huwa fī al-dayri ilā al-āna
sentences.l: and he said to them: Did you set-free this ascetic, or is he in the monastery up to the now?
sentences.i: And he said to them, “Did you rescue this ascetic, or is he still in the monastery?”

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا بَلْ خَلَّصْنَاهُ وَقَتَلْنَا صَاحِبَ الدَّيْرِ مِنْ خَوْفِنَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِنَا ثُمَّ أَسْرَعْنَا فِى الْهَرَبِ خَوْفًا مِنَ الْعَطَبِ وَقَدْ أَخْبَرَنَا بَعْضُ الثِّقَاتِ أَنَّ فِي هَذَا الدَّيْرِ قَنَاطِيرَ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْجَوَاهِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū bal khallaṣnāhu wa-qatalnā ṣāḥiba al-dayri min khawfinā ʿalā anfusinā thumma asraʿnā fī al-harabi khawfan mina al-ʿaṭabi wa-qad akhbaranā baʿḍu al-thiqāti anna fī hādhā al-dayri qanāṭīra mina al-dhahabi wa-al-fiḍḍati wa-al-jawāhiri
sentences.l: And they said: Nay, we set-him-free, and we killed the master of the monastery, from our fear for ourselves; then we hastened in the flight, for fear of the ruin; and some of the trustworthy-ones have told us that in this monastery are qinṭārs of the gold and the silver and the jewels.
sentences.i: “Indeed we rescued him,” they said, “and killed the master of the monastery, fearing for our own lives; then we fled in haste, for fear of destruction. And men we trust have told us that this monastery holds hundredweights of gold and silver and jewels.”
sentences.n: Sajʿ: harab/ʿaṭab, “flight/destruction”. A qinṭār is a large weight, roughly a hundredweight; the plural qanāṭīr is the Qurʾān's word for heaped treasure (Q 3:14). The mention of the treasure is bait: the crone means to draw the Muslim army to the monastery.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَتَوْا بِالصُّنْدُوقِ وَأَخْرَجُوا مِنْهُ تِلْكَ الْمَلْعُونَةَ كَأَنَّهَا قَرْنُ خِيَارِ شَنْبَرٍ مِنْ شِدَّةِ السَّوَادِ وَالنُّحُولِ وَهِيَ مُكَبَّلَةٌ بِتِلْكَ السَّلَاسِلِ وَالْقُيُودِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika ataw bi-al-ṣundūqi wa-akhrajū minhu tilka al-malʿūnata ka-annahā qarnu khiyāri shanbarin min shiddati al-sawādi wa-al-nuḥūli wa-hiya mukabbalatun bi-tilka al-salāsili wa-al-quyūdi
sentences.l: Then after that they brought the chest and brought-out from it that accursed-one, as-if she were a pod of khiyār shanbar from the intensity of the blackness and the leanness, and she bound-in-fetters with those chains and the shackles.
sentences.i: After that they brought the chest and took out of it that accursed woman, as black and shrivelled as a cassia pod, still loaded with the chains and fetters.
sentences.n: khiyār shanbar is the cassia tree (Cassia fistula), whose long, hard pods are almost black; qarn, “horn”, is the pod. ataw bi-, “came with”, is “brought”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَهَا ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هُوَ وَالْحَاضِرُونَ ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ خِيَارِ الْعُبَّادِ وَأَفْضَلِ الزُّهَّادِ خُصُوصًا وَجَبِينُهَا يُضِيءُ مِنَ الدِّهَانِ الَّذِي دَهَنَتْ بِهِ وَجْهَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarahā ḍawʾu al-makāni huwa wa-al-ḥāḍirūna ẓannū annahu rajulun min khiyāri al-ʿubbādi wa-afḍali al-zuhhādi khuṣūṣan wa-jabīnuhā yuḍīʾu mina al-dihāni alladhī dahanat bihi wajhahā
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw her, he and the present-ones, they thought that he was a man of the choicest of the worshippers and the most-excellent of the ascetics, especially as her brow shone from the ointment with which she had anointed her face.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān and all who were present saw her, they took her for a man, one of the choicest of worshippers and the best of ascetics, the more so as her forehead shone with the ointment she had rubbed on her face.
sentences.n: The narrator calls her “her”, but the onlookers take her for a man: annahu, “that he was”. A shining brow was the mark of the devout, as if lit by prayer; hers shines with grease. Sajʿ: ʿubbād/zuhhād. khiyār, “the choicest”, is the same word as in khiyār shanbar just before, a play the print probably intends. naẓara here takes its object directly, “saw her”.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخُوهُ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا ثُمَّ قَامَا إِلَيْهَا وَقَبَّلَا يَدَيْهَا وَرِجْلَيْهَا وَصَارَا يَنْتَحِبَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-bakā ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-akhūhu bukāʾan shadīdan thumma qāmā ilayhā wa-qabbalā yadayhā wa-rijlayhā wa-ṣārā yantaḥibāni
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother wept a weeping severe, then the two rose to her and kissed her two hands and her two feet, and the two began sobbing.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother wept bitterly; then they rose, went to her, kissed her hands and her feet, and fell to sobbing.
sentences.n: The print has بكاو, a misprint for بكاء, corrected here: bukāʾan shadīdan, “a severe weeping”, the verb's own noun used to intensify it. ṣārā with a following verb, “they became doing”, is “they began to”.

sentences.t: فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِمَا وَقَالَتْ كُفَّا عَنْ هَذَا الْبُكَاءِ وَاسْمَعَا كَلَامِي
sentences.tr: fa-ashārat ilayhimā wa-qālat kuffā ʿan hādhā al-bukāʾi wa-ismaʿā kalāmī
sentences.l: And she signed to the two of them and said: Hold-back, you two, from this weeping, and hear, you two, my speech.
sentences.i: She motioned to them and said, “Stop this weeping, both of you, and listen to what I have to say.”

sentences.t: فَتَرَكَا الْبُكَاءَ امْتِثَالًا لِأَمْرِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-tarakā al-bukāʾa imtithālan li-amrihā
sentences.l: And the two left the weeping, in compliance with her command.
sentences.i: They stopped weeping, as she had bidden them.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ اعْلَمَا أَنِّي قَدْ رَضِيتُ بِمَا صَنَعَهُ بِي مَوْلَايَ لِأَنِّي أَرَى أَنَّ الْبَلَاءَ الَّذِي نَزَلَ بِي امْتِحَانٌ مِنْهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati iʿlamā annī qad raḍītu bi-mā ṣanaʿahu bī mawlāya li-annī arā anna al-balāʾa alladhī nazala bī imtiḥānun minhu ʿazza wa-jalla
sentences.l: And she said: Know, you two, that I have been content with what my Lord did to me, because I see that the affliction which came-down on me is a trial from Him, mighty and majestic is He.
sentences.i: Then she said, “Know that I am content with what my Lord has done to me, for I see that the affliction that has come upon me is a trial sent by Him, the Mighty and Glorious.
sentences.n: mawlāy, “my master”, is God here. ʿazza wa-jalla, “mighty and majestic is He”, is said after naming God, as taʿālā is.

sentences.t: وَمَنْ لَمْ يَصْبِرْ عَلَى الْبَلَاءِ وَالْمِحَنِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ وُصُولٌ إِلَى جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ
sentences.tr: wa-man lam yaṣbir ʿalā al-balāʾi wa-al-miḥani fa-laysa lahu wuṣūlun ilā jannāti al-naʿīmi
sentences.l: And whoever does not endure-patiently the affliction and the trials, then there is not for him an arrival at the Gardens of the Bliss.
sentences.i: Whoever does not bear affliction and trial with patience will never reach the Gardens of Bliss.
sentences.n: jannāt al-naʿīm, “the Gardens of Bliss”, is a Qurʾānic name of Paradise (e.g. Q 10:9).

sentences.t: وَكُنْتُ أَتَمَنَّى أَنِّي أَعُودُ إِلَى بِلَادِي لَا جَزَعاً مِنَ الْبَلَاءِ الَّذِي حَلَّ بِي بَلْ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ أَمُوتَ تَحْتَ حَوَافِرِ خَيْلِ الْمُجَاهِدِينَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ بَعْدَ الْقَتْلِ أَحْيَاءٌ غَيْرُ أَمْوَاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kuntu atamannā annī aʿūdu ilā bilādī lā jazaʿan mina al-balāʾi alladhī ḥalla bī bal li-ajli an amūta taḥta ḥawāfiri khayli al-mujāhidīna alladhīna hum baʿda al-qatli aḥyāʾun ghayru amwātin
sentences.l: And I used to wish that I return to my country, not in impatience from the affliction which alighted on me, but for the sake of that I die under the hooves of the horses of the strivers, who are, after the killing, living, not dead.
sentences.i: I used to wish that I might return to my own country, not because I could not bear the affliction that had befallen me, but so that I might die beneath the hooves of the horses of the holy warriors, who after they are slain are alive and not dead.”
sentences.n: After tamannā the print has annī aʿūdu, “that I return”, where Classical usage would write an aʿūda; read as printed. The fighters who are “alive, not dead” after being killed echo Q 3:169: “Do not think those slain in the way of God dead; rather they are alive with their Lord.” Her cover is that of a Muslim ascetic carried off by the Christians, so “my country” is the land of Islam.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma anshadat hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then she recited these lines:
sentences.i: Then she recited these lines:

sentences.t:
اَلْحِصْنُ طُوْرٌ وَنَارُ الْحَرْبِ مُوْقَدَةٌ * وَاَنْتَ مُوْسَى وَهٰذَا الْوَقْتُ مِيْقَاتُ
اَلْقِ الْعَصَا تَتَلَقَّفْ كُلَّ مَا صَنَعُوْا * وَلَا تَخَفْ بِحِبَالِ الْقَوْمِ حَيَّاتُ
فَاقْرَأْ سُطُوْرَ الْعِدَى يَوْمَ الْوَغَى سُوْرًا * فَاِنَّ سَيْفَكَ فِى الْاَعْنَاقِ آيَاتُ
sentences.tr:
al-ḥiṣnu ṭūrun wa-nāru al-ḥarbi mūqadatun * wa-anta mūsā wa-hādhā al-waqtu mīqātu
alqi al-ʿaṣā tatalaqqaf kulla mā ṣanaʿū * wa-lā takhaf bi-ḥibāli al-qawmi ḥayyātu
fa-iqraʾ suṭūra al-ʿidā yawma al-waghā sūran * fa-inna sayfaka fī al-aʿnāqi āyātu
sentences.l:
The fortress is a Ṭūr, and the fire of the war kindled, * and you are Moses, and this the time is an appointed-time.
Cast the staff: it will swallow up all that they made, * and do not fear: in the ropes of the people are snakes.
So read the lines of the enemies on the day of the battle as sūras, * for your sword, on the necks, is verses.
sentences.i:
The fortress is a Sinai, and the fire of war is lit, * and you are Moses, and this is your appointed hour.
Cast down your staff, and it will swallow all their works, * and do not fear, though the people's ropes are snakes.
Read the enemy's ranks on the day of battle as sūras, * for your sword writes its verses on their necks.
sentences.n: The print has فاترأ, a misprint for فاقرأ, “so read”, corrected here; the rest of the verse is copied with the print's own pointing. Each line borrows from the Qurʾānic story of Moses: the fire on Mount Ṭūr (Sinai) and the appointed time (mīqāt) at which God met him (Q 20:10, 7:143), the staff that swallowed up what Pharaoh's sorcerers had made (Q 7:117, 20:69), and their ropes that seemed to be snakes (Q 20:66). The last line plays on writing: suṭūr are lines of script and also ranks of men; sūr are the sūras of the Qurʾān, and āyāt both its verses and signs or wonders. The print points tatalaqqaf with two tāʾs where the Qurʾān has talqaf; the second line's ḥayyātu is read as a sentence of its own, “in the ropes of the people are snakes”. Sung by a Christian crone to Muslim kings, the poem is her bait: it urges them to attack.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتِ الْعَجُوزُ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا تَنَاثَرَتْ مِنْ عَيْنَيْهَا الْمَدَامِعُ وَجَبِينُهَا بِالدِّهَانِ كَالضَّوْءِ اللَّامِعِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghati al-ʿajūzu min shiʿrihā tanātharat min ʿaynayhā al-madāmiʿu wa-jabīnuhā bi-al-dihāni ka-al-ḍawʾi al-lāmiʿi
sentences.l: And when the old woman had finished from her verse, there scattered from her two eyes the tears, and her forehead, with the oil, like the light, the gleaming.
sentences.i: When the old woman had finished her verses, the tears fell scattering from her eyes, while her forehead, rubbed with oil, shone like a gleaming light.
sentences.n: wa-jabīnuhā, “and her forehead”, opens a circumstantial clause with no verb: “her forehead being, with the oil, like gleaming light”. The crone has oiled her brow so that it shines like the face of one worn with prayer. Sajʿ: madāmiʿ/lāmiʿ.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهَا شَرْكَانُ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَهَا وَأَحْضَرَلَهَا الطَّعَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma ilayhā sharrukānu wa-qabbala yadahā wa-aḥḍara lahā al-ṭaʿāma
sentences.l: So Sharrukān rose to her and kissed her hand and had-brought for her the food,
sentences.i: Sharrukān rose and went to her, kissed her hand, and had food brought for her;
sentences.n: واحضرلها is printed as one word, wa-aḥḍara lahā, “and he brought for her”.

sentences.t: فَامْتَنَعَتْ وَقَالَتْ إِنِّي لَمْ أُفْطِرْ مِنْ مُدَّةِ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ عَامًا فَكَيْفَ أُفْطِرُ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ وَقَدْ جَادَ عَلَيَّ الْمَوْلَى بِالْخَلَاصِ مِنْ أَسْرِ الْكُفَّارِ وَدَفَعَ عَنِّي مَا هُوَ أَشَقُّ مِنْ عَذَابِ النَّارِ فَأَنَا أَصْبِرُ إِلَى الْغُرُوبِ
sentences.tr: fa-imtanaʿat wa-qālat innī lam ufṭir min muddati khamsata ʿashara ʿāman fa-kayfa ufṭiru fī hādhihi al-sāʿati wa-qad jāda ʿalayya al-mawlā bi-al-khalāṣi min asri al-kuffāri wa-dafaʿa ʿannī mā huwa ashaqqu min ʿadhābi al-nāri fa-anā aṣbiru ilā al-ghurūbi
sentences.l: but she refused and said: I have not broken-fast for a space of fifteen years; so how shall I break-fast in this hour, when the Master has been-generous to me with the deliverance from the captivity of the unbelievers, and has pushed away from me what is harder than the torment of the Fire? So I will be-patient until the sunset.
sentences.i: but she refused, saying, “I have not broken my fast these fifteen years. How should I break it at this hour, when the Lord has granted me the bounty of deliverance from captivity among the unbelievers, and has turned from me a thing harder to bear than the torment of hellfire? I will hold out until sunset.”
sentences.n: She claims to keep a perpetual daytime fast, eating only after sunset. jāda ʿalā … bi-, “be generous to someone with”: bi- marks the gift. Sajʿ: kuffār/nār. al-mawlā, “the Master”, is God.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَاءَ وَقْتُ الْعِشَاءِ أَقْبَلَ شَرْكَانُ هُوَ وَضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَقَدَّمَا إِلَيْهَا الْأَكْلَ وَقَالَا لَهَا كُلْ أَيُّهَا الزَّاهِدُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāʾa waqtu al-ʿishāʾi aqbala sharrukānu huwa wa-ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-qaddamā ilayhā al-akla wa-qālā lahā kul ayyuhā al-zāhidu
sentences.l: And when the time of the nightfall came, Sharrukān came-forward, he and Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and the two set-before her the eating, and the two said to her: Eat, O the ascetic!
sentences.i: When nightfall came, Sharrukān and Ḍawʾ al-Makān came to her together and set the food before her, saying, “Eat, holy man.”
sentences.n: The kings still take her for a man: kul, “eat”, and al-zāhid, “the ascetic”, are both masculine, while the narrator says lahā, “to her”. The dual qaddamā, qālā, “the two of them set, said”, follows the pair of brothers.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ مَا هَذَا وَقْتُ الْأَكْلِ وَإِنَّمَا هَذَا وَقْتُ عِبَادَةِ الْمَلِكِ الدَّيَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat mā hādhā waqtu al-akli wa-innamā hādhā waqtu ʿibādati al-maliki al-dayyāni
sentences.l: And she said: This is not the time of the eating; this is only the time of the worship of the King, the Judge.
sentences.i: But she said, “This is no time for eating; this is the time for worshipping the King who judges all.”
sentences.n: mā here negates a noun sentence: mā hādhā waqtu, “this is not the time”. al-Dayyān, “the Judge”, the One who requites, is a name of God.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْتَصَبَتْ فِى الْمِحْرَابِ تُصَلِّي إِلَى أَنْ ذَهَبَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: thumma intaṣabat fī al-miḥrābi tuṣallī ilā an dhahaba al-laylu
sentences.l: Then she stood-upright in the prayer-niche, praying, until the night went.
sentences.i: Then she took her stand in the prayer niche and prayed until the night was gone.
sentences.n: The miḥrāb is the niche that shows the direction of prayer.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تَزَلْ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ بِلَيَالِيهَا وَهِيَ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ إِلَّا وَقْتَ التَّحِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam tazal ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati thalāthata ayyāmin bi-layālīhā wa-hiya lam tafʿal illā waqta al-taḥiyyati
sentences.l: And she did not cease upon this state three days with their nights, and she did not do [so] except at the time of the greeting.
sentences.i: She kept on in this way for three days and their nights, and did not do so except at the hour of the salutation.
sentences.n: The last clause is doubtful as printed: lam tafʿal illā waqta al-taḥiyya, “she did not do [it] except at the time of the greeting”, is kept and translated as it stands. The likeliest sense is that she broke off only for the salutation (al-taḥiyya, the greeting said at the close of a prayer); the print may instead mean لم تفطر, “she did not break her fast except at the time of the greeting”. bi-layālīhā, “with their nights”: bi- joins the nights to the days. ثلٰثة is printed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَهَا ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ مَلَكَ قَلْبَهُ حُسْنُ الِاعْتِقَادِ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾahā ḍawʾu al-makāni ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati malaka qalbahu ḥusnu al-iʿtiqādi fīhā
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw her upon that state, there possessed his heart the goodness of the belief in her,
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw her so, his heart was won by a firm faith in her holiness,
sentences.n: رأها, without the long ā, is the edition’s spelling of رآها, raʾāhā, “he saw her”. ḥusn al-iʿtiqād fī, “good belief in”, is trust in someone’s sanctity.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِشَرْكَانَ اضْرِبْ خَيْمَةً مِنَ الْأَدِيمِ لِذَلِكَ الْعَابِدِ وَوَكِّلْ فَرَّاشًا بِخِدْمَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-sharrukāna iḍrib khaymatan mina al-adīmi li-dhālika al-ʿābidi wa-wakkil farrāshan bi-khidmatihi
sentences.l: and he said to Sharrukān: Pitch a tent of the leather for that worshipper, and charge a tent-servant with his service.
sentences.i: and he said to Sharrukān, “Pitch a tent of leather for this holy man, and set a servant to wait on him.”
sentences.n: ḍaraba khayma, “strike a tent”, is to pitch it. wakkala … bi-, “put someone in charge of”: bi- marks the charge. The farrāsh spreads the carpets and keeps the tent.

sentences.t: وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ دَعَتْ بِالطَّعَامِ فَقَدَّمُوا لَهَا مِنَ الْأَلْوَانِ مَا تَشْتَهِى الْأَنْفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi daʿat bi-al-ṭaʿāmi fa-qaddamū lahā mina al-alwāni mā tashtahī al-anfusu wa-taladhdhu al-aʿyunu
sentences.l: And on the day, the fourth, she called for the food, and they set before her of the colours what the souls desire and the eyes delight-in;
sentences.i: On the fourth day she called for food, and they set before her dishes of every kind, all that souls could desire and eyes delight in;
sentences.n: daʿā bi-, “call for”: the verb takes bi- for the thing sent for. alwān, “colours”, are dishes of different kinds. “What souls desire and eyes delight in” is the Qurʾān’s phrase for the delights of Paradise (43:71).

sentences.t: فَلَمْ تَأْكُلْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ إِلَّا رَغِيفًا وَاحِدًا بِمِلْحٍ ثُمَّ نَوَتِ الصَّوْمَ
sentences.tr: fa-lam taʾkul min dhālika kullihi illā raghīfan wāḥidan bi-milḥin thumma nawati al-ṣawma
sentences.l: but she did not eat of that all of it except one loaf with salt; then she intended the fast.
sentences.i: but of all of it she ate nothing but a single loaf with salt, and then she made her intention to fast.
sentences.n: nawā al-ṣawm, “intend the fast”: a fast must be declared by an intention (niyya) the night before.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا جَاءَ اللَّيْلُ قَامَتْ إِلَى الصَّلٰوةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā jāʾa al-laylu qāmat ilā al-ṣalāti
sentences.l: And when the night came, she rose to the prayer
sentences.i: And when night came, she rose to pray
sentences.n: الصلٰوة is printed in the old spelling with wāw and the dagger alif, for ṣalāh, “prayer”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ أَمَّا هَذَا الرَّجُلُ فَقَدْ زَهِدَ الدُّنْيَا غَايَةَ الزُّهْدِ وَلَوْلَا هَذَا الْجِهَادُ لَكُنْتُ لَازَمْتُهُ وَأَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ بِخِدْمَتِهِ حَتَّى أَلْقَاهُ وَقَدِ اشْتَهَيْتُ أَنْ أَدْخُلَ مَعَهُ الْخَيْمَةَ وَأَتَحَدَّثَ مَعَهُ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu li-ḍawʾi al-makāni ammā hādhā al-rajulu fa-qad zahida al-dunyā ghāyata al-zuhdi wa-lawlā hādhā al-jihādu la-kuntu lāzamtuhu wa-aʿbudu allāha bi-khidmatihi ḥattā alqāhu wa-qadi ishtahaytu an adkhula maʿahu al-khaymata wa-ataḥaddatha maʿahu sāʿatan
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: As for this man, he has renounced the world to the utmost of the renouncing; and were it not for this holy-war, I would have kept-close to him, and I would worship God by the serving of him until I meet Him. And I have longed to go in with him into the tent and talk with him an hour.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān, “As for this man, he has renounced the world as completely as a man can. Were it not for this holy war, I would stay by him always and worship God by serving him until the day I meet my Lord. I have been longing to go into his tent with him and talk with him for a while.”
sentences.n: ḥattā alqāhu, “until I meet Him”: the pronoun is God, met at death. lawlā … la-kuntu, “were it not for … I would have”: the standard unreal condition. aʿbudu is imperfect after la-kuntu lāzamtuhu, “and I would be worshipping”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَنَا كَذَلِكَ وَلَكِنْ نَحْنُ فِي غَدٍ ذَاهِبُونَ إِلَى غَزْوِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَنَا سَاعَةً مِثْلَ هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-anā ka-dhālika wa-lākin naḥnu fī ghadin dhāhibūna ilā ghazwi al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-lam najid lanā sāʿatan mithla hādhihi al-sāʿati
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: And I likewise; but we tomorrow are going to the raiding of Constantinople, and we did not find for us an hour like this hour.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān answered, “So do I. But tomorrow we march against Constantinople, and we may never find another hour like this one.”
sentences.n: lam najid, formally “we did not find”, here looks forward: “we will find no other hour like this”, so the visit must be now.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَأَنَا الْآخَرُ أَشْتَهِي أَنْ أَرَى هَذَا الزَّاهِدَ لَعَلَّهُ يَدْعُو لِي بِقَضَاءِ نَحْبِي فِى الْجِهَادِ وَلِقَاءِ رَبِّي فَإِنِّي زَهِدْتُ الدُّنْيَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru dandānu wa-anā al-ākharu ashtahī an arā hādhā al-zāhida laʿallahu yadʿū lī bi-qaḍāʾi naḥbī fī al-jihādi wa-liqāʾi rabbī fa-innī zahidtu al-dunyā
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān said: And I the other long to see this ascetic; perhaps he will pray for me for the fulfilling of my vow in the holy-war and the meeting of my Lord, for I have renounced the world.
sentences.i: And the vizier Dandān said, “I too long to see this holy man. Perhaps he will pray that I may die fighting in the holy war and meet my Lord, for I have done with this world.”
sentences.n: wa-anā al-ākhar, “and I the other”, is colloquial for “I too”. qaḍāʾ al-naḥb, “fulfilling one's vow”, echoes the Qurʾān (33:23) on believers who kept their pledge to the death, and means dying in battle.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِمُ اللَّيْلُ دَخَلُوا عَلَى تِلْكَ الْكَاهِنَةِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي فِي خَيْمَتِهَا فَرَأَوْهَا قَائِمَةً تُصَلِّي فَدَنَوْا مِنْهَا وَصَارُوا يَبْكُونَ رَحْمَةً لَهَا وَهِيَ لَا تَلْتَفِتُ إِلَيْهِمْ إِلَى أَنِ انْتَصَفَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā janna ʿalayhimu al-laylu dakhalū ʿalā tilka al-kāhinati dhāti al-dawāhī fī khaymatihā fa-raʾawhā qāʾimatan tuṣallī fa-danaw minhā wa-ṣārū yabkūna raḥmatan lahā wa-hiya lā taltafitu ilayhim ilā ani intaṣafa al-laylu
sentences.l: And when the night darkened upon them, they went in upon that soothsayer Dhāt al-Dawāhī in her tent, and they saw her standing praying; and they drew-near to her and began weeping in pity for her, while she did not turn to them, until the night was halved.
sentences.i: When night had fallen over them, they went in to that sorceress Dhāt al-Dawāhī in her tent and found her standing at prayer. They came close to her and began to weep for pity of her, but she paid them no heed until midnight.
sentences.n: al-kāhina is properly a pagan soothsayer or priestess: the narrator, who knows the truth, names her for what she is, while the kings still take her for a holy man. janna al-layl ʿalā, “night covered”, is the Qurʾānic phrase for nightfall (6:76).

sentences.t: فَسَلَّمَتْ مِنْ صَلٰوتِهَا ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَحَيَّتْهُمْ وَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ لِمَا ذَا جِئْتُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-sallamat min ṣalātihā thumma aqbalat ʿalayhim wa-ḥayyathum wa-qālat lahum li-mā dhā jiʾtum
sentences.l: Then she said-the-salutation out of her prayer, then turned toward them and greeted them and said to them: For what have you come?
sentences.i: Then she closed her prayer with the salutation of peace, turned to them, greeted them, and asked, “Why have you come?”
sentences.n: sallama min al-ṣalāh is to end the ritual prayer with the closing al-salāmu ʿalaykum. صلٰوتها is printed with the dagger alif, ṣalātihā. لما ذا is printed as two words, li-mā dhā, “why”.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهَا أَيُّهَا الْعَابِدُ أَمَا سَمِعْتَ بُكَائِنَا حَوْلَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahā ayyuhā al-ʿābidu a-mā samiʿta bukāʾinā ḥawlaka
sentences.l: And they said to her: O you the worshipper, did you not hear our weeping around you?
sentences.i: They said to her, “O holy man, did you not hear us weeping all around you?”
sentences.n: They address her in the masculine, al-ʿābid, “the worshipper”, since she is disguised as a man; the narrator keeps “her”. بكائنا is the object of samiʿta, and Classical would write and read it bukāʾanā; the print's spelling on a yāʾ-seat gives bukāʾinā, a common Middle Arabic habit with hamza.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِنَّ الَّذِي يَقِفُ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ لَا يَكُونُ لَهُ وُجُودٌ فِى الْكَوْنِ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ صَوْتَ أَحَدٍ أَوْ يَرَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat inna alladhī yaqifu bayna yadayi allāhi lā yakūnu lahu wujūdun fī al-kawni ḥattā yasmaʿa ṣawta aḥadin aw yarāhu
sentences.l: And she said: Truly, he who stands between the two hands of God, there is not for him an existence in the world, so that he should hear the voice of anyone or see him.
sentences.i: She said, “Whoever stands before God has no being left in this world, so that he might hear anyone's voice or see anyone.”
sentences.n: bayna yaday, “between the two hands of”, is “in the presence of”. The claim is the Sufi one of self-extinction in prayer: the worshipper ceases to exist to the world.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّنَا نَشْتَهِي أَنْ تُحَدِّثَنَا بِسَبَبِ أَسْرِكَ وَتَدْعُوَ لَنَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ فَإِنَّهَا خَيْرٌ لَنَا مِنْ مُلْكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum qālū innanā nashtahī an tuḥaddithanā bi-sababi asrika wa-tadʿuwa lanā fī hādhihi al-laylati fa-innahā khayrun lanā min mulki al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: Then truly they said: We long that you tell us of the cause of your captivity, and pray for us in this night; for it is better for us than the dominion of Constantinople.
sentences.i: Then they said, “We long for you to tell us how you came to be taken captive, and to pray for us this night; for that is worth more to us than the rule of Constantinople.”
sentences.n: thumma innahum qālū, “then they said”: the inna is a narrative filler of this style, not emphasis. ḥaddatha bi-, “tell (someone) of”: the verb takes bi- for the thing told.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُمْ قَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ لَوْلَا أَنَّكُمْ أُمَرَاءُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مَا أُحَدِّثُكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَبَدًا فَإِنِّي لَا أَشْكُو إِلَّا إِلَى اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahum qālat wa-allāhi lawlā annakum umarāʾu al-muslimīna mā uḥaddithukum bi-shayʾin min dhālika abadan fa-innī lā ashkū illā ilā allāhi
sentences.l: And when she heard their speech, she said: By God, were it not that you are the commanders of the Muslims, I would not tell you of a thing of that ever; for I do not complain except to God.
sentences.i: When she heard what they said, she answered, “By God, were you not the princes of the Muslims, I would never tell you a word of it; for I make my complaint to God alone.”
sentences.n: lā ashkū illā ilā allāh echoes Jacob in the Qurʾān (12:86): “I complain of my grief and sorrow only to God.” الّا is printed with its shadda.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِسَبَبِ أَسْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā ukhbirukum bi-sababi asrī
sentences.l: And here I am telling you of the cause of my captivity.
sentences.i: But now I will tell you how I came to be taken captive.

sentences.t: اعْلَمُوا أَنَّنِي كُنْتُ فِى الْقُدْسِ مَعَ بَعْضِ الْأَبْدَالِ وَأَرْبَابِ الْأَحْوَالِ وَكُنْتُ لَا أَتَكَبَّرُ عَلَيْهِمْ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى أَنْعَمَ عَلَيَّ بِالتَّوَاضُعِ وَالزُّهْدِ
sentences.tr: iʿlamū annanī kuntu fī al-qudsi maʿa baʿḍi al-abdāli wa-arbābi al-aḥwāli wa-kuntu lā atakabbaru ʿalayhim li-anna allāha subḥānahu wa-taʿālā anʿama ʿalayya bi-al-tawāḍuʿi wa-al-zuhdi
sentences.l: Know that I was in Jerusalem with some of the Substitutes and the lords of the states, and I did not use to be-proud over them, because God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, had favoured me with the humility and the renunciation.
sentences.i: Know that I was in Jerusalem with certain of the Abdāl and the masters of mystic states, and I never set myself above them, for God, glory be to Him, the Exalted, had blessed me with humility and detachment from the world.
sentences.n: The abdāl, “substitutes”, are in Sufi lore a fixed number of hidden saints by whom the world is upheld; when one dies God puts another in his place. arbāb al-aḥwāl, “lords of the states”, are mystics who receive the aḥwāl, God-given spiritual states. Sajʿ: abdāl/aḥwāl. anʿama ʿalā … bi-, “favour someone with”: bi- names the gift. عليّ is printed with its shadda.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّنِي تَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ لَيْلَةً وَمَشَيْتُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ فَدَاخَلَنِي الْعُجْبُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا أَدْرِي وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي مَنْ مِثْلِي يَمْشِي عَلَي الْمَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa annanī tawajjahtu ilā al-baḥri laylatan wa-mashaytu ʿalā al-māʾi fa-dākhalanī al-ʿujbu min ḥaythu lā adrī wa-qultu fī nafsī man mithlī yamshī ʿalā al-māʾi
sentences.l: And it chanced that I went to the sea one night and walked upon the water; and the self-admiration entered into me from where I did not know, and I said in my soul: Who is like me, walking upon the water?
sentences.i: Now it happened one night that I went down to the sea and walked upon the water, and pride crept into me before I knew it, and I said to myself, ‘Who is like me, who can walk upon the water?’
sentences.n: al-ʿujb is self-admiration, the spiritual pride that undoes a saint's miracle; the word is ʿujb here, not ʿajab, “wonder”. The second علي, “on”, is printed with yāʾ for ʿalā.

sentences.t: فَقَسَا قَلْبِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ وَابْتَلَانِي اللَّهُ بِحُبِّ السَّفَرِ فَسَافَرْتُ إِلَى بِلَادِ الرُّومِ وَجُلْتُ فِي أَقْطَارِهَا سَنَةً كَامِلَةً حَتَّى لَمْ أَتْرُكْ مَوْضِعًا إِلَّا عَبَدْتُ اللَّهَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qasā qalbī min dhālika al-waqti wa-ibtalānī allāhu bi-ḥubbi al-safari fa-sāfartu ilā bilādi al-rūmi wa-jultu fī aqṭārihā sanatan kāmilatan ḥattā lam atruk mawḍiʿan illā ʿabadtu allāha fīhi
sentences.l: And my heart grew-hard from that time, and God tried me with the love of the travel; so I travelled to the lands of the Rūm and roamed in its regions a year complete, until I did not leave a place except I worshipped God in it.
sentences.i: From that hour my heart grew hard, and God afflicted me with a love of travel; so I journeyed to the land of the Rūm and wandered through its provinces for a whole year, until there was no place left in which I had not worshipped God.
sentences.n: The hardening of the heart is the punishment for the pride of the moment before, when the ascetic walked on the water and thought, “Who is like me?” ibtalā bi-, “try someone with”: bi- names the affliction sent.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلْتُ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ صَعِدْتُ إِلَى هَذَا الْجَبَلِ وَفِيهِ دَيْرُ رَاهِبٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ مَطْرُوحَنَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣaltu ilā hādhā al-makāni ṣaʿidtu ilā hādhā al-jabali wa-fīhi dayru rāhibin yuqālu lahu maṭrūḥanā
sentences.l: And when I arrived at this place, I climbed to this mountain, and in it is a monastery of a monk who is called Maṭrūḥanā.
sentences.i: When I came to this place I climbed this mountain, where there is the monastery of a monk called Maṭrūḥanā.
sentences.n: yuqālu lahu, “it is said to him”, is the ordinary way of saying “called”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي خَرَجَ إِلَيَّ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَيَّ وَرِجْلَيَّ فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُكَ مُنْذُ دَخَلْتَ بِلَادَ الرُّومِ وَقَدْ شَوَّقْتَنِي إِلَى بِلَادِ الْإِسْلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī kharaja ilayya wa-qabbala yadayya wa-rijlayya fa-qāla innī raʾaytuka mundhu dakhalta bilāda al-rūmi wa-qad shawwaqtanī ilā bilādi al-islāmi
sentences.l: And when he saw me, he came out to me and kissed my two hands and my two feet, and said: I have seen you since you entered the lands of the Rūm, and you have made-me-long for the lands of Islam.
sentences.i: When he saw me he came out to me and kissed my hands and my feet, and said, ‘I have watched you ever since you entered the land of the Rūm, and you have filled me with longing for the lands of Islam.’
sentences.n: يدي ورجلي are read here as duals, yadayya wa-rijlayya, “my two hands and my two feet”; the letters would also allow the singular. The monk's warmth is a pretence, as what follows shows.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَخَذَ بِيَدِي وَأَدْخَلَنِي ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرَ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ بِي إِلَى بَيْتٍ مُظْلِمٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu akhadha bi-yadī wa-adkhalanī dhālika al-dayra thumma dakhala bī ilā baytin muẓlimin
sentences.l: Then he took by my hand and made-me-enter that monastery, then entered with me into a room, dark.
sentences.i: Then he took me by the hand and led me into the monastery, and brought me into a dark room.
sentences.n: akhadha bi-yadihi, “took him by the hand”: bi- marks what is taken hold of. dakhala bi-, “enter with”, is “bring in”. bayt here is a room, not a house.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ فِيهِ غَافَلَنِي وَأَغْلَقَ عَلَيَّ الْبَابَ وَتَرَكَنِي فِيهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا مِنْ غَيْرِ طَعَامٍ وَلَا شَرَابٍ وَكَانَ قَصْدُهُ بِذَلِكَ قَتْلِي صَبْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu fīhi ghāfalanī wa-aghlaqa ʿalayya al-bāba wa-tarakanī fīhi arbaʿīna yawman min ghayri ṭaʿāmin wa-lā sharābin wa-kāna qaṣduhu bi-dhālika qatlī ṣabran
sentences.l: And when I entered into it, he caught-me-off-guard and shut upon me the door, and left me in it forty days without food and without drink; and his intent by that was the killing of me by-confinement.
sentences.i: As soon as I was inside, he caught me off my guard, locked the door on me, and left me there forty days without food or drink, meaning by it that I should die a slow death.
sentences.n: The print has قصدة, a misprint for قصده, corrected here. ghāfala, to catch someone unawares. qatalahu ṣabran, to kill someone by holding him fast; here, by shutting him up to starve.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرَ بَطْرِيقٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ دَقْيَانُوسُ وَمَعَهُ عَشَرَةٌ مِنَ الْغِلْمَانِ وَمَعَهُ ابْنَةٌ يُقَالُ لَهَا تَمَاثِيلُ وَلَكِنَّهَا فِى الْحُسْنِ لَيْسَ لَهَا مَثِيلٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa fī baʿḍi al-ayyāmi annahu dakhala dhālika al-dayra baṭrīqun yuqālu lahu daqyānūsu wa-maʿahu ʿasharatun mina al-ghilmāni wa-maʿahu ibnatun yuqālu lahā tamāthīlu wa-lākinnahā fī al-ḥusni laysa lahā mathīlun
sentences.l: And it chanced on one of the days that there entered that monastery a patrician who is called Daqyānūs, and with him ten of the pages, and with him a daughter who is called Tamāthīl — but she, in the beauty, there is not for her a like.
sentences.i: Then one day it happened that a patrician called Daqyānūs came to the monastery with ten of his pages, and with him a daughter named Tamāthīl, who in beauty had no equal.
sentences.n: Tamāthīl means “images, statues”, and rings against mathīl, “equal”. The ghilmān are young men in a great man's service, pages or retainers.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا الدَّيْرَ أَخْبَرَهُمُ الرَّاهِبُ مَطْرُوحَنَى بِخَبَرِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalū al-dayra akhbarahumu al-rāhibu maṭrūḥanā bi-khabarī
sentences.l: And when they entered the monastery, the monk Maṭrūḥanā informed them of my news.
sentences.i: When they had come into the monastery, the monk Maṭrūḥanā told them about me.
sentences.n: akhbara bi-, “inform of”: the verb takes bi- for the thing told.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْبَطْرِيقُ أَخْرِجُوهُ لِأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْ لَحْمِهِ مَا يَأْكُلُهُ الطَّيْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-baṭrīqu akhrijūhu li-annahu lam yabqa min laḥmihi mā yaʾkuluhu al-ṭayru
sentences.l: And the patrician said: Bring-him-out, because there has not remained of his flesh what the birds would eat.
sentences.i: The patrician said, ‘Bring him out, for there is not flesh enough left on him to feed the birds.’
sentences.n: The print has بأكله, a misprint for يأكله, corrected here. After forty days without food the patrician expects a corpse.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحُوا بَابَ ذَلِكَ الْبَيْتِ الْمُظْلِمِ فَوَجَدُونِي مُنْتَصِبًا فِى الْمِحْرَابِ أُصَلِّي وَأَقْرَأُ وَأُسَبِّحُ وَأَتَضَرَّعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥū bāba dhālika al-bayti al-muẓlimi fa-wajadūnī muntaṣiban fī al-miḥrābi uṣallī wa-aqraʾu wa-usabbiḥu wa-ataḍarraʿu ilā allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And they opened the door of that room, the dark one, and found me standing-upright in the prayer-niche, praying and reciting and glorifying and humbly-entreating God, exalted is He.
sentences.i: They opened the door of the dark room and found me standing upright in the prayer niche, praying, reciting, glorifying God and humbly beseeching Him, exalted is He.
sentences.n: The miḥrāb is the niche that marks the direction of prayer: a Muslim's prayer niche inside a Christian monastery is part of the wonder the ascetic claims. taʿālā, “He is exalted”, follows the name of God as a formula.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَؤُنِي عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ قَالَ مَطْرُوحَنَى إِنَّ هَذَا سَاحِرٌ مِنَ السَّحَرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾūnī ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati qāla maṭrūḥanā inna hādhā sāḥirun mina al-saḥarati
sentences.l: And when they saw me in that state, Maṭrūḥanā said: Truly this is a sorcerer of the sorcerers.
sentences.i: When they saw me like that, Maṭrūḥanā said, ‘This man is a sorcerer, one of the magicians!’
sentences.n: رؤني is the print's spelling of raʾawnī, “they saw me”, without the wāw of the plural; it is pointed here as it stands.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعُوا كَلَامَهُ قَامُوا جَمِيعًا وَدَخَلُوا عَلَيَّ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيَّ دَقْيَانُوسُ هُوَ وَجَمَاعَتُهُ وَضَرَبُونِي ضَرْبًا عَنِيفًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿū kalāmahu qāmū jamīʿan wa-dakhalū ʿalayya wa-aqbala ʿalayya daqyānūsu huwa wa-jamāʿatuhu wa-ḍarabūnī ḍarban ʿanīfan
sentences.l: And when they heard his speech, they rose all-together and came-in upon me, and Daqyānūs advanced upon me, he and his company, and they beat me a beating, violent.
sentences.i: When they heard what he said they all rose and came in on me; Daqyānūs and his men fell upon me and beat me savagely.
sentences.n: dakhala ʿalā, “come in upon”, is to enter where someone is. ḍarabūnī ḍarban ʿanīfan, “beat me a violent beating”: the verbal noun with its adjective gives the manner.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَمَنَّيْتُ الْمَوْتَ وَلُمْتُ نَفْسِي وَقُلْتُ هَذَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَتَكَبَّرُ وَيُعْجَبُ بِمَا أَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِ رَبُّهُ مِمَّالَيْسَ فِي طَاقَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika tamannaytu al-mawta wa-lumtu nafsī wa-qultu hādhā jazāʾu man yatakabbaru wa-yuʿjabu bi-mā anʿama ʿalayhi rabbuhu mimmā laysa fī ṭāqatihi
sentences.l: And at that I wished-for the death, and blamed my soul, and said: This is the reward of whoever is-proud and is-pleased-with-himself over what his Lord bestowed upon him, of what is not in his power.
sentences.i: At that I longed for death and reproached myself, and said, ‘This is the reward of anyone who grows proud and vain over the favours his Lord has granted him, which were never in his own power.
sentences.n: مماليس is printed as one word: mimmā laysa, “of what is not”. uʿjiba bi-, “be pleased with, vain of”: bi- names the thing one is vain of. The favour meant is the walking on water.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتِ يَا نَفْسِي قَدْ دَاخَلَكِ الْعُجْبُ وَالْكِبْرُ
sentences.tr: wa-anti yā nafsī qad dākhalaki al-ʿujbu wa-al-kibru
sentences.l: And you, O my soul, there have entered-into-you the self-admiration and the pride.
sentences.i: And you, my soul: vanity and pride have crept into you.
sentences.n: nafs, “soul, self”, is feminine, so it is addressed as anti, with -ki for “you”.

sentences.t: أَمَا عَلِمْتِ أَنَّ الْكِبْرَ يُغْضِبُ الرَّبَّ وَيُقَسِّى الْقَلْبَ وَيُدْخِلُ الْإِنْسَانَ النَّارَ
sentences.tr: a-mā ʿalimti anna al-kibra yughḍibu al-rabba wa-yuqassī al-qalba wa-yudkhilu al-insāna al-nāra
sentences.l: Did you not know that the pride angers the Lord and hardens the heart and makes the man enter the Fire?
sentences.i: Did you not know that pride angers the Lord, hardens the heart, and brings a man into the Fire?’
sentences.n: al-nār, “the Fire”, is Hell.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَيَّدُونِي وَرَدُّونِي إِلَى مَكَانِي وَكَانَ سِرْدَابًا فِي ذَلِكَ الْبَيْتِ تَحْتَ الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika qayyadūnī wa-raddūnī ilā makānī wa-kāna sirdāban fī dhālika al-bayti taḥta al-arḍi
sentences.l: Then after that they fettered me and returned me to my place, and it was an underground-vault in that room, under the earth.
sentences.i: After that they put me in fetters and took me back to my place, which was a vault in that room, beneath the ground.

sentences.t: وَكُلَّ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ يَرْمُونَ إِلَيَّ قُرْصَةً مِنَ الشَّعِيرِ وَشَرْبَةَ مَاءٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kulla thalāthati ayyāmin yarmūna ilayya qurṣatan mina al-shaʿīri wa-sharbata māʾin
sentences.l: And every three days they throw to me a round-loaf of the barley and a drink of water.
sentences.i: Every three days they would throw me a round of barley bread and a draught of water.
sentences.n: kulla, “every”, is accusative of time. ثلٰثة is printed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَكُلَّ شَهْرٍ أَوْ شَهْرَيْنِ يَأْتِى الْبَطْرِيقُ وَيَدْخُلُ ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرَ
sentences.tr: wa-kulla shahrin aw shahrayni yaʾtī al-baṭrīqu wa-yadkhulu dhālika al-dayra
sentences.l: And every month or two months the patrician comes and enters that monastery.
sentences.i: Every month or two the patrician comes and visits the monastery.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ كَبِرَتِ ابْنَتُهُ تَمَاثِيلُ لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ بِنْتَ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ حِينَ رَأَيْتُهَا وَمَضَى لِي فِى الْأَسْرِ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً فَجُمْلَةُ عُمْرِهَا أَرْبَعَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ عَامًا
sentences.tr: wa-qad kabirati ibnatuhu tamāthīlu li-annahā kānat binta tisʿi sinīna ḥīna raʾaytuhā wa-maḍā lī fī al-asri khamsa ʿashrata sanatan fa-jumlatu ʿumrihā arbaʿatun wa-ʿishrūna ʿāman
sentences.l: And his daughter Tamāthīl has grown-up, because she was a girl of nine years when I saw her, and there have passed for me in the captivity fifteen years; so the sum of her age is four and twenty years.
sentences.i: His daughter Tamāthīl is grown now: she was a girl of nine when I first saw her, and I have spent fifteen years in captivity, so she is twenty-four years old in all.
sentences.n: li-annahā, “because”, gives the ground for saying so (“she must be grown, for …”), not the cause of her growing. maḍā lī, “there passed for me”: li- marks whose years they were.

sentences.t: وَلَيْسَ فِي بِلَادِنَا وَلَا فِى بِلَادِ الرُّومِ أَحْسَنُ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-laysa fī bilādinā wa-lā fī bilādi al-rūmi aḥsanu minhā
sentences.l: And there is not in our lands nor in the lands of the Rūm one more-beautiful than her.
sentences.i: In neither our lands nor the land of the Rūm is there anyone more beautiful than she.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَبُوهَا يَخَافُ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْمَلِكِ أَنْ يَأْخُذَهَا مِنْهُ لِأَنَّهَا وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلْمَسِيحِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna abūhā yakhāfu ʿalayhā mina al-maliki an yaʾkhudhahā minhu li-annahā wahabat nafsahā li-al-masīḥi
sentences.l: And her father was fearing for her from the king, lest he take her from him, because she has given herself to the Messiah;
sentences.i: Her father lives in fear that the king will take her from him, for she has vowed herself to Christ;
sentences.n: khāfa ʿalā, “fear for”, and khāfa min, “fear (someone)”, both stand here. wahabat nafsahā li-al-masīḥ, “she gave herself to the Messiah”: she has vowed herself to Christ as a virgin.

sentences.t: غَيْرَأَنَّهَا تَرْكَبُ مَعَ أَبِيهَا فِي زِيِّ الرِّجَالِ الْفُرْسَانِ وَلَيْسَ لَهَا مَثِيلٌ فِى الْحُسْنِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ مَنْ رَآهَا أَنَّهَا جَارِيَةٌ
sentences.tr: ghayra annahā tarkabu maʿa abīhā fī ziyyi al-rijāli al-fursāni wa-laysa lahā mathīlun fī al-ḥusni wa-lam yaʿlam man raʾāhā annahā jāriyatun
sentences.l: except that she rides with her father in the garb of the men, the horsemen; and there is not for her a like in the beauty, and whoever sees her does not know that she is a girl.
sentences.i: only she rides out with her father dressed as a knight, and though she has no equal in beauty, no one who sees her knows she is a girl.
sentences.n: The print has جاربة, a misprint for جارية, corrected here. غيرانها is printed as one word: ghayra annahā, “except that she”. jāriya, often “slave girl”, is here simply “girl, young woman”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَزَنَ أَبُوهَا أَمْوَالَهَا فِي هَذَا الدَّيْرِ لِأَنَّ كُلَّ مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ شَئٌ مِنْ نَفَائِسِ الذَّخَائِرِ يَضَعُهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad khazana abūhā amwālahā fī hādhā al-dayri li-anna kulla man kāna ʿindahu shayʾun min nafāʾisi al-dhakhāʾiri yaḍaʿuhu fī dhālika al-dayri
sentences.l: And her father has stored her riches in this monastery, because every one who had with him a thing of the precious-ones of the treasures puts it in that monastery.
sentences.i: Her father has stored her riches in this monastery, for anyone who owns something of precious treasure lays it up there.
sentences.n: شئ is the print's spelling of shayʾ, “thing”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْجَوَاهِرِ وَسَائِرِ الْأَوَانِي وَالتُّحَفِ مَا لَا يُحْصِي عَدَدَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: wa-qad raʾaytu fīhi min anwāʿi al-dhahabi wa-al-fiḍḍati wa-al-jawāhiri wa-sāʾiri al-awānī wa-al-tuḥafi mā lā yuḥṣī ʿadadahu illā allāhu taʿālā
sentences.l: And I have seen in it, of the kinds of the gold and the silver and the jewels and the rest of the vessels and the rarities, what none counts its number except God, exalted is He.
sentences.i: I have seen in it gold and silver and jewels of every kind, and vessels and rare treasures of all sorts, more than anyone but God, exalted is He, could count.
sentences.n: min … mā: the min, “of”, names beforehand what the mā, “what”, is made up of.

sentences.t: فَأَنْتُمْ أَوْلَى بِهِ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ الْكَفَرَةِ فَخُذُوا مَا فِي هَذَا الدَّيْرِ وَأَنْفِقُوهُ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَخُصُوصًا الْمُجَاهِدِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-antum awlā bihi min hāʾulāʾi al-kafarati fa-khudhū mā fī hādhā al-dayri wa-anfiqūhu ʿalā al-muslimīna wa-khuṣūṣan al-mujāhidīna
sentences.l: So you are more-entitled to it than these unbelievers; so take what is in this monastery and spend it on the Muslims, and especially the strivers-in-holy-war.
sentences.i: You have a better right to it than these infidels: take what is in this monastery and spend it on the Muslims, above all on those who fight in the holy war.
sentences.n: awlā bi-, “having the better claim to”: bi- marks what is claimed.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا وَصَلَ هَؤُلَاءِ التُّجَّارُ إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَبَاعُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ كَلَّمَتْهُمْ تِلْكَ الصُّورَةُ الَّتِي فِى الْحَائِطِ لِكَرَامَةٍ أَكْرَمَنِى اللَّهُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lammā waṣala hāʾulāʾi al-tujjāru ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-bāʿū biḍāʿatahum kallamathum tilka al-ṣūratu allatī fī al-ḥāʾiṭi li-karāmatin akramanī allāhu bihā
sentences.l: And when these merchants arrived at Constantinople and sold their merchandise, that image which is on the wall spoke to them, by a grace with which God graced me;
sentences.i: When these merchants reached Constantinople and had sold their goods, the picture on the wall spoke to them, by a miracle God granted me in His favour;
sentences.n: A karāma is a wonder God grants a saint, as against the muʿjiza of a prophet; li- gives the cause, “by virtue of”. akrama bi-, “honour with”: bi- names the gift. The talking picture is the one the merchants spoke of in the night before.

sentences.t: فَجَاؤُا إِلَى ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرِ وَقَتَلُوا الْبَطْرِيقَ مَطْرُوحَنَى بَعْدَ أَنْ عَاقَبُوهُ أَشَدَّ الْعِقَابِ وَجَرُّوهُ مِنْ لِحْيَتِهِ فَدَلَّهُمْ عَلَى مَوْضِعِي
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾū ilā dhālika al-dayri wa-qatalū al-baṭrīqa maṭrūḥanā baʿda an ʿāqabūhu ashadda al-ʿiqābi wa-jarrūhu min liḥyatihi fa-dallahum ʿalā mawḍiʿī
sentences.l: and they came to that monastery and killed the patrician Maṭrūḥanā, after they had punished him the hardest of the punishment and dragged him by his beard, and he guided them to my place.
sentences.i: so they came to the monastery and killed the patrician Maṭrūḥanā, after they had punished him most cruelly and dragged him by the beard, so that he showed them where I was.
sentences.n: The print calls the man killed al-baṭrīq, “the patrician”; he is the monk Maṭrūḥanā, and the word is kept as printed. فجاؤا is the print's spelling of jāʾū, “they came”. jarra min, “drag by”: min marks where he was seized.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذُونِي وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ سَبِيلٌ إِلَّا الْهَرَبَ خَوْفًا مِنَ الْعَطَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhūnī wa-lam yakun lahum sabīlun illā al-haraba khawfan mina al-ʿaṭabi
sentences.l: And they took me, and there was not for them a way except the flight, in-fear of the ruin.
sentences.i: They took me with them, and had no course but to flee for fear of destruction.
sentences.n: khawfan, “out of fear”, is an accusative of cause. Rhyme: harab/ʿaṭab.

sentences.t: وَفِى لَيْلَةِ غَدٍ تَأْتِي تَمَاثِيلُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرِ عَلَى عَادَتِهَا وَيَلْحَقُهَا أَبُوهَا مَعَ غِلْمَانِهِ لِأَنَّهُ يَخَافُ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-fī laylati ghadin taʾtī tamāthīlu ilā dhālika al-dayri ʿalā ʿādatihā wa-yalḥaquhā abūhā maʿa ghilmānihi li-annahu yakhāfu ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And in the night of tomorrow Tamāthīl comes to that monastery according to her custom, and her father follows-her with his pages, because he fears for her.
sentences.i: Tomorrow night Tamāthīl will come to the monastery as she always does, and her father will follow her with his pages, for he fears for her.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ شِئْتُمْ أَنْ تُشَاهِدُوا هَذَا الْأَمْرَ فَخُذُونِي بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَنَا أُسَلِّمُ إِلَيْكُمُ الْأَمْوَالَ وَخِزَانَةَ الْبَطْرِيقِ دَقْيَانُوسَ الَّتِي فِي ذَلِكَ الْجَبَلِ
sentences.tr: fa-in shiʾtum an tushāhidū hādhā al-amra fa-khudhūnī bayna aydīkum wa-anā usallimu ilaykumu al-amwāla wa-khizānata al-baṭrīqi daqyānūsa allatī fī dhālika al-jabali
sentences.l: So if you wish to witness this matter, then take me between your hands, and I will hand-over to you the riches and the treasury of the patrician Daqyānūs which is in that mountain.
sentences.i: If you wish to see this for yourselves, take me along before you, and I will hand over to you the riches and the treasure-house of the patrician Daqyānūs that lies in that mountain.
sentences.n: bayna aydīkum, “between your hands”, is “before you, in your company”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَأَيْتُهُمْ يُخْرِجُونَ أَوَانِى الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ يَشْرَبُونَ فِيهَا وَرَأَيْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ جَارِيَةً تُغَنِّي لَهُمْ بِالْعَرَبِيِّ
sentences.tr: wa-qad raʾaytuhum yukhrijūna awānī al-dhahabi wa-al-fiḍḍati yashrabūna fīhā wa-raʾaytu ʿindahum jāriyatan tughannī lahum bi-al-ʿarabiyyi
sentences.l: And I have seen them bringing-out vessels of the gold and the silver, drinking in them, and I saw with them a slave-girl singing to them in the Arabic.
sentences.i: I have seen them bring out vessels of gold and silver to drink from, and I saw with them a slave girl who sang to them in Arabic.
sentences.n: Drinking from vessels of gold and silver is forbidden to Muslims, so the detail paints the Christians' luxury for the ascetic's hearers. bi-al-ʿarabiyy, “in Arabic”: bi- names the language.

sentences.t: فَوَا حَسْرَتَاهُ لَوْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ الصَّوْتُ الْحَسَنُ فِي قِرَاءَةِ الْقُرْآنِ
sentences.tr: fa-wā ḥasratāhu law kāna dhālika al-ṣawtu al-ḥasanu fī qirāʾati al-qurʾāni
sentences.l: So O my-grief! If that voice, the beautiful one, were in the reading of the Qurʾān!
sentences.i: Oh, the pity of it! If only that lovely voice were given to reciting the Qurʾān!
sentences.n: فوا حسرتاه is printed as two words: fa-wā ḥasratāhu, “oh, alas!”, the lament particle wā with the lament ending -āh. law here voices a wish and has no answering clause.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ شِئْتُمْ فَادْخُلُوا ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرَ وَاكْمُنُوا فِيهِ إِلَى أَنْ يَصِلَ دَقْيَانُوسُ وَمَعَهُ ابْنَتُهُ فَخُذُوهَا فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَصْلُحُ إِلَّا لِمَلِكِ الزَّمَانِ شَرْكَانَ أَوْ لِلْمَلِكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-in shiʾtum fa-udkhulū dhālika al-dayra wa-ukmunū fīhi ilā an yaṣila daqyānūsu wa-maʿahu ibnatuhu fa-khudhūhā fa-innahā lā taṣluḥu illā li-maliki al-zamāni sharrukāna aw li-al-maliki ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: And if you wish, then enter that monastery and lie-in-ambush in it until Daqyānūs arrives, and with him his daughter; then take her, for she is not fit except for the king of the age, Sharrukān, or for King Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: If you like, go into the monastery and lie in wait there until Daqyānūs comes with his daughter; then seize her, for she is fit for no one but Sharrukān, king of the age, or King Ḍawʾ al-Makān.”
sentences.n: This is the end of the old woman's false tale. kamana, “lie hidden in ambush”. Daqyānūs is the Arabic form of Decius, the persecuting emperor of the legend of the Sleepers of the Cave; the tale gives the name to a Christian lord.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحُوا بِذَلِكَ حِينَ سَمِعُوا كَلَامَهَا إِلَّا الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يُصَدِّقْهَا وَمَا دَخَلَ كَلَامُهَا فِي عَقْلِهِ وَخَشِيَ أَنْ يَتَحَدَّثَ مَعَهَا لِأَجْلِ خَاطِرِ الْمَلِكِ وَصَارَ بَاهِتًا مِنْ كَلَامِهَا وَيَلُوحُ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ عَلَامَةُ الْإِنْكَارِ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥū bi-dhālika ḥīna samiʿū kalāmahā illā al-wazīra dandāna fa-innahu lam yuṣaddiqhā wa-mā dakhala kalāmuhā fī ʿaqlihi wa-khashiya an yataḥaddatha maʿahā li-ajli khāṭiri al-maliki wa-ṣāra bāhitan min kalāmihā wa-yalūḥu ʿalā wajhihi ʿalāmatu al-inkāri ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And they rejoiced at that when they heard her speech, except the vizier Dandān, for he did not believe her, and her speech did not enter into his mind; and he feared to talk with her for the sake of the feelings of the king, and he became dumbfounded at her speech, and there gleams on his face the sign of the disavowal of her.
sentences.i: They were all delighted when they heard her, all but the vizier Dandān: he did not believe her, and her words found no room in his mind. Yet he shrank from challenging her, out of regard for the king, and stood bewildered at what she said, his disbelief plain on his face.
sentences.n: li-ajli khāṭiri al-maliki, “for the sake of the king's mind”: khāṭir is the heart's feeling, and the phrase means out of consideration for him. inkār ʿalā is refusing to accept what someone says. yalūḥu, a present tense in past narrative, paints the scene: the sign “keeps showing”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُقْبِلَ الْبَطْرِيقُ وَيَنْظُرَ هَذِةِ الْعَسَاكِرَ فِى الْمَرْجِ فَمَا يَجْسُرُأَنْ يَدْخُلَ الدَّيْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu dhātu al-dawāhī innī akhāfu an yuqbila al-baṭrīqu wa-yanẓura hādhihi al-ʿasākira fī al-marji fa-mā yajsuru an yadkhula al-dayra
sentences.l: And the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī said: I fear that the patrician may come-on and see these armies in the meadow, and then he will not dare to enter the monastery.
sentences.i: Then the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī said, “I am afraid that the patrician will come and see all these troops in the meadow, and then he will not dare to go into the monastery.”
sentences.n: يجسران is printed as one word: yajsuru an, “he dares to”. هذة for هذه is the print's habit. The patrician is presumably Daqyānūs, whose coming she has just announced.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ السُّلْطَانُ الْعَسْكَرَأَنْ يَرْحَلُوا صَوْبَ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-sulṭānu al-ʿaskara an yarḥalū ṣawba al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: So the sultan commanded the army that they should march toward Constantinople.
sentences.i: So the sultan ordered the army to march on toward Constantinople.
sentences.n: العسكران is printed as one word: al-ʿaskara an, “the army that”. The verb is plural, yarḥalū, because the army is many men.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِنَّ قَصْدِي أَنْ نَأْخُذَ مَعَنَا مِائَةَ فَارِسٍ وَبِغَالًا كَثِيرَةً وَنَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى ذَلِكَ الْجَبَلِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ نُحَمِّلَهُمُ الْمَالَ الَّذِى فِى الدَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni inna qaṣdī an naʾkhudha maʿanā miʾata fārisin wa-bighālan kathīratan wa-natawajjaha ilā dhālika al-jabali li-ajli an nuḥammilahumu al-māla alladhī fī al-dayri
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: My intention is that we take with us a hundred horsemen and many mules, and head to that mountain, for the sake of that we load them with the wealth that is in the monastery.
sentences.i: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “My plan is to take a hundred horsemen with us and a great many mules and make for that mountain, so that we can load them with the treasure in the monastery.”
sentences.n: nuḥammilahum, “that we load them”: the mules are referred to with the human plural -hum, as Middle Arabic often does. li-ajli an, “for the sake of that”, is simply “so that”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ إِلَى الْحَاجِبِ الْكَبِيرِ فَأَحْضَرَهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَحْضَرَ الْمُقَدَّمِينَ وَالْأَتْرَاكَ وَالدَّيْلَمَ
sentences.tr: thumma arsala min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi ilā al-ḥājibi al-kabīri fa-aḥḍarahu bayna yadayhi wa-aḥḍara al-muqaddamīna wa-al-atrāka wa-al-daylama
sentences.l: Then he sent, from his time and his hour, to the great chamberlain, and had him brought between his two hands, and had brought the commanders and the Turks and the Daylam,
sentences.i: Then he sent at once for the chief chamberlain and had him brought before him, and he summoned the commanders, the Turks and the Daylamites,
sentences.n: min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi, “from his time and his hour”: at once. bayna yadayhi, “between his two hands”: into his presence. The Daylam are highlanders of northern Iran serving in the Muslim army.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ إِذَا كَانَ وَقْتُ الصَّبَاحِ فَارْحَلُوا إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَأَنْتَ أَيُّهَا الْحَاجِبُ عِوَضًا عَنِّي فِى الرَّأْيِ وَالتَّدْبِيرِ وَأَنْتَ يَا رُسْتُمُ تَكُونُ نَائِبًا عَنْ أَخِي فِى الْقِتَالِ وَلَا تُعْلِمُوا أَحَدًا أَنَّنَا لَسْنَا مَعَكُمْ وَبَعْدَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ نَلْحَقُكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla idhā kāna waqtu al-ṣabāḥi fa-irḥalū ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-anta ayyuhā al-ḥājibu ʿiwaḍan ʿannī fī al-raʾyi wa-al-tadbīri wa-anta yā rustumu takūnu nāʾiban ʿan akhī fī al-qitāli wa-lā tuʿlimū aḥadan annanā lasnā maʿakum wa-baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin nalḥaqukum
sentences.l: and said: When it is the time of morning, march to Constantinople; and you, O chamberlain, a substitute for me in the counsel and the management; and you, O Rustam, you shall be deputy for my brother in the fighting; and do not let anyone know that we are not with you; and after three days we will overtake you.
sentences.i: and said, “When morning comes, march for Constantinople. You, chamberlain, shall stand in my place in counsel and command, and you, Rustam, shall act for my brother in battle. Let no one know that we are not with you; in three days we will catch up with you.”
sentences.n: wa-anta ayyuhā al-ḥājibu ʿiwaḍan ʿannī: the verb is left unsaid, and ʿiwaḍan is accusative as if after takūnu, “you shall be”, which the next clause supplies. tuʿlimū, “let know”, is the causative (form IV) of ʿalima, “know”. ثلٰثة is printed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْتَخَبَ مِائَةَ فَارِسٍ مِنَ الْأَبْطَالِ وَانْحَازَ هُوَ وَأَخُوهُ شَرْكَانُ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَالْمِائَةُ فَارِسٍ وَأَخَذُوا مَعَهُمُ الْبِغَالَ وَالصَّنَادِيقَ لِأَجْلِ حَمْلِ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma intakhaba miʾata fārisin mina al-abṭāli wa-inḥāza huwa wa-akhūhu sharrukānu wa-al-wazīru dandānu wa-al-miʾatu fārisin wa-akhadhū maʿahumu al-bighāla wa-al-ṣanādīqa li-ajli ḥamli al-māli
sentences.l: Then he chose a hundred horsemen of the champions, and he drew-apart, he and his brother Sharrukān and the vizier Dandān and the hundred horsemen, and they took with them the mules and the chests for the sake of the carrying of the wealth.
sentences.i: Then he picked a hundred horsemen from among the bravest, and he went off apart, he and his brother Sharrukān and the vizier Dandān with the hundred horsemen, taking the mules and the chests to carry away the treasure.
sentences.n: inḥāza, “draw aside, separate oneself”. wa-al-miʾatu fārisin, “and the hundred horsemen”: the article goes on the numeral, the everyday usage; strict Classical grammar would have miʾatu al-fārisi.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night.
